+Follow the [discoverable unavailable-feature pattern](../design-philosophy/SKILL.md#make-unavailable-features-understandable): a feature promoted in documentation should not become inexplicably absent solely because the user cannot enable it. Announce both the disabled state and its reason using the control's supported ARIA semantics; a grey label, briefcase icon, or hover alone is insufficient. Keep icons decorative when text already conveys their meaning.

+Explanatory links must remain independently mouse- and keyboard-operable without activating the disabled option. Verify actual Tab/Shift+Tab and Enter behavior, not just `tabIndex` or a programmatic `focus()`; list navigation may skip disabled rows. Preserve focus/selection on policy refresh, guard stale actions, and update the feature's accessibility help with the available explanation and next step. Reuse the settings, model, harness, and permission-picker examples linked in the design guidance.

+Users look for features they have seen in release notes, documentation, or promotion. Silently removing an otherwise relevant option when policy, account entitlement, setup, or version requirements prevent its use makes the product feel broken. Prefer keeping it discoverable but disabled, with a concise, truthful reason and a useful next step.

+- Distinguish **blocked by organization policy**, **requires sign-in/upgrade/update**, **not supported here**, and **still loading** using authoritative state; absence from a list alone is not evidence of policy.

+- Reuse existing disabled-row styling and the briefcase indicator for managed policy. Provide a visible reason or independently actionable **Learn why** link; do not make hover the only way to discover the explanation.

+- Presentation must not grant access: block pointer, keyboard, and stale-menu activation while keeping explanatory links operable. Follow the [accessibility guidance](../accessibility/SKILL.md#explaining-unavailable-options).

+- This is not a blanket rule to expose everything. Preserve explicit feature-hiding choices (including disabled AI), unsupported provider capabilities, and unreleased feature gates. Explain unavailable features where they are relevant without inventing support or exposing sensitive policy values.
+Reuse these patterns rather than copying entire implementations:
+| Model picker | [Unavailable models with distinct admin, upgrade, and update explanations](../../../src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/input/modelPicker/modelPickerItemPrimitives.ts) |
+| Harness picker | [Availability descriptions and policy help links](../../../src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/sessionTypeAvailability.ts) |

+| Permissions picker | [Shared permission-level policy presentation](../../../src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostModePickerPresentation.ts) and [picker integration](../../../src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostChatInputPicker.ts), with [runtime policy boundaries](../policy-and-managed-settings/sdk-runtime-policy.md) |
> - **See:** a toolbar sits on a solid filled bar, separator lines between every button, the buttons pushed up against each other.

- The VS Code settings-to-managed-settings bridge is a compatibility path for legacy settings only. Do not add a new VS Code setting in order to bridge it; define new runtime-owned controls directly in the managed-settings/SDK contract. The bridge itself is unconditional; do not reintroduce a compatibility gate for it.
- Run `npm run export-policy-data` for every VS Code or extension policy change. Never edit `build/lib/policies/policyData.jsonc` manually.

+Users should be able to understand why a feature described in release notes or documentation is unavailable. Prefer an otherwise relevant option remaining visible but disabled, with the standard briefcase managed-policy indicator, localized explanation, and accessible next step, rather than silently filtering it out. Follow the [shared design guidance and settings/model/permission-picker examples](../design-philosophy/SKILL.md#make-unavailable-features-understandable).

+Use authoritative policy provenance to distinguish prohibited options from unsupported capabilities, feature gates, and pending state. Keep presentation separate from authorization: showing Assisted or Allow All as disabled must never put a prohibited value back into the runtime's allowed enum or bypass create/resume/write validation. Test policy refresh/removal, keyboard and pointer activation, stale menus, and independent help links; preserve explicit AI-hiding behavior.
